docs.title: Welcome to bolt.diy
docs.text:
bolt.diy is an open-source AI developer workspace for building web applications in the browser. Choose a model provider for each prompt, work with project files in the integrated editor and terminal, and preview the running app. The application supports 22+ cloud and local providers. OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are enabled by default; enable and configure other providers under Settings → Providers.

For the current feature summary and command reference, see the repository README. For setup troubleshooting, see the FAQ.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Browser-based development with an editor, terminal, and live preview powered by WebContainers
  • Model selection across supported cloud and local providers
  • Image and file attachments for prompts
  • Project workflows including GitHub import/push, ZIP export, snapshots, and visual diffs
  • MCP tools that can be selected for a prompt
  • Supabase integration for connected projects
  • Deployment integrations for Netlify, Vercel, and GitHub Pages
  • Electron desktop app and Docker-based development/deployment options
  • Prompt library, voice prompting, and configurable workspace settings

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git, if you plan to clone the repository
  • Node.js 22.12.0 or later
  • pnpm 9.15.9 or later
  • Docker, if you plan to use the container setup

The supported Node.js and pnpm versions are defined in package.json.

docs.title: Configure providers
docs.text:
You can set provider credentials in the application or in a local environment file.

To use environment variables, copy .env.example to .env.local, replace the placeholders for the providers you use, and remove or comment out unused placeholders. For example:

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_key_here
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here
GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY=your_key_here
OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY=your_key_here
OLLAMA_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434
LMSTUDIO_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1234

In the app, enable a provider under Settings → Providers. Select it in the chat composer, choose Edit API Key, enter the key, and save. Keys entered in the UI are stored in JavaScript-accessible browser cookies and sent to the application server with requests; protect browser access and use HTTPS for remote deployments. A key status indicator means a key is set, not that the provider has validated it.

For OpenRouter's free router, select OpenRouter as the provider and Free Models Router (openrouter/free) as the model. Model availability and rate limits are controlled by OpenRouter. For Ollama or LM Studio running on the host while bolt.diy runs in Docker, use a host-reachable endpoint such as host.docker.internal; 127.0.0.1 inside the container refers to the container itself.

Never commit .env.local or .env files. Docker Compose uses .env for variable substitution and passes both .env and .env.local to the container. After configuring .env.local, run ./scripts/setup-env.sh or copy it to .env; repeat this after changing .env.local.

docs.title: Run the development server
docs.text:
pnpm run dev

Open http://localhost:5173. Use a current browser with WebContainer support; some browser features may require a secure context.

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
Configure the environment files as described above, then run:

docker compose --profile development up

For production image builds, use pnpm run dockerbuild:prod and docker compose --profile production up. See the repository Docker Compose configuration for the available services and ports.

docs.title: Working with projects
docs.text:
Describe the framework or stack you want in your first prompt. When a matching starter is available, bolt.diy can import it and then continue implementing your request. A starter is only a starting point: review the generated files and check that the app runs in the preview.

You can select configured MCP tools from the attachment menu beside the prompt composer. To use Supabase, connect the service and select a project in the chat interface before asking bolt.diy to work with it.

Project import, push, and deployment options depend on the service connection and project compatibility. Manage service connections under Settings → Integrations → Connectors. Use the in-app deployment flow for provider-specific instructions and status.

docs.title: Add a provider
docs.text: Providers are implemented as classes in app/lib/modules/llm/providers/ and exported from app/lib/modules/llm/registry.ts. Extending BaseProvider alone does not register a provider; include it in the registry. Follow the patterns in existing provider files and check the current BaseProvider and ModelInfo types before implementing a new integration, since the provider interface can change.

docs.title: Development commands
docs.text:
Common commands from the repository root:

Command Purpose pnpm run dev Start the development server pnpm run build Build the app for production pnpm run preview Build and preview locally pnpm run typecheck Run TypeScript type checking pnpm run lint Run ESLint pnpm test Run the Vitest suite pnpm run test:e2e Run Playwright end-to-end tests pnpm run dockerbuild Build the development Docker image pnpm run dockerbuild:prod Build the production Docker image pnpm run deploy Build and deploy to Cloudflare Workers

For contribution steps, see the Contributing Guide. For the full set of scripts, consult package.json.

docs.title: Contributing to bolt.diy
docs.text: Contributions are welcome. Please read the repository's Contributing Guide for project-specific expectations before opening an issue or pull request.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Requirements: Node.js 22.12.0 or later and pnpm 9.15.9 or later. The supported versions are declared in package.json.

git clone https://github.com/stackblitz-labs/bolt.diy.git
cd bolt.diy
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env.local

Edit .env.local with credentials for providers you plan to use; remove or comment out unused placeholders. Never commit .env.local or .env. Docker Compose uses both .env and .env.local; run ./scripts/setup-env.sh after configuring .env.local and again after changing it.

Start the development server with:

pnpm run dev

Then open http://localhost:5173.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Choose checks relevant to your change. These commands are defined in the repository's package.json:

pnpm run lint
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run test:e2e

The unit/integration/performance suite is run with pnpm test; Playwright end-to-end tests are a separate command.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
• Use a focused branch and keep the change scoped to a clear issue or feature.
  • Include enough context in the PR description to explain the change and how you checked it.
  • Update documentation when behavior or setup instructions change.
  • Link related issues and address review feedback.

For deployment and Docker commands, refer to the repository README and the checked-in Docker Compose configuration. Those files are the source of truth as the project evolves.

docs.title: Models and setup
docs.text:
Which models should I use?

Model availability and capability change over time. Browse the model list for your configured provider in the application. For coding, choose a model with strong code skills and enough context for your project; use a smaller model when speed or cost matters. Local providers such as Ollama and LM Studio are options when you want to run models on your own machine.

How do I configure an API key?

In the app, enable a provider under Settings → Providers, select it in the chat composer, choose Edit API Key, and save the key. You can also set supported provider variables in .env.local at the repository root. The key indicator only means that a key is stored; it does not validate the key with the provider.

Keys entered in the UI are stored in JavaScript-accessible browser cookies and sent to the application server with requests. Protect access to the browser and use HTTPS when exposing the app remotely. Never commit .env.local or .env files.

How do I use Ollama or LM Studio with Docker?

Set OLLAMA_API_BASE_URL or LMSTUDIO_API_BASE_URL to an address reachable from the container. Inside Docker, 127.0.0.1 points to the container. On supported systems, use a host address such as host.docker.internal.

How do I use OpenRouter's free model router?

Choose OpenRouter in the provider selector and Free Models Router (openrouter/free) in the model selector. Availability and rate limits are controlled by OpenRouter.

docs.title: Projects and integrations
docs.text:
How do I start with a particular framework?

Mention the framework or stack in your first prompt. When a matching starter is available, bolt.diy can import it and continue with your requested changes. Starters can change over time; review the generated project and check the preview after the build.

How do I use MCP tools?

Configure an MCP server under Settings → MCP Servers. Then open the attachment menu beside the prompt composer and select the tools you want available for that prompt. Only select tools from servers you trust.

How do I connect Supabase?

Connect Supabase and select a project from the chat interface before asking bolt.diy to work with its database. Database setup and credentials are managed through that connection; the app's WebContainer does not include the Supabase CLI.

How do I import or publish a project?

Connect the relevant service under Settings → Integrations → Connectors. Available project and deployment actions depend on the service and project. Follow the in-app flow for connection, permissions, and deployment status. You can also export a project as a ZIP.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
A request fails with an API key error

Confirm the provider is enabled and selected, and that the key is present in the provider's Edit API Key dialog or in the server environment. A stored-key indicator does not confirm provider-side validity. Check the provider's account status and the app/server logs for the response details.

The preview is blank or does not load

Check the terminal for install or development-server errors, confirm that the expected development server is running, and inspect the browser console. Some WebContainer features require a supported browser and secure context. Refreshing the preview can help after the server starts, but fix any reported build errors first.

A local provider cannot be reached from Docker

The address 127.0.0.1 inside the container refers to the container. Set the provider base URL to an address reachable from Docker, such as host.docker.internal where supported, and confirm the provider accepts connections from that host.

Docker Compose reports a missing variable or env file

Compose needs both .env and .env.local. Copy .env.example to .env.local, configure the variables you need, and run ./scripts/setup-env.sh to prepare .env. Repeat this after changing .env.local; shell environment variables can override Compose substitution values.

An MCP server does not connect

Check the server URL, authentication settings, and server logs. Confirm the server is running and reachable from the application environment, then retry the connection.

The app does not start locally

Check that Node.js and pnpm meet the versions in package.json, reinstall dependencies with pnpm install, and review the terminal output. For current setup commands, see the documentation home and repository README.

docs.title: Contributing and support
docs.text:
How do I contribute or report an issue?

Read the Contributing Guide. Report bugs or request features through the GitHub issue tracker.

Where can I find the roadmap?

See the project's public roadmap. Model and integration support may change between releases, so use the current app and repository documentation for up-to-date details.
